stories.title: E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: E Ink, an originator, pioneer and global commercial leader in ePaper technology, broke ground on the expansion of its U.S. headquarters in Billerica, MA. The project expands the footprint at the company’s Billerica Innovation Center, which is home to 260-plus E Ink employees and serves as a key global R&D center. “Expanding our Billerica campus strengthens our ability to advance technology innovation in the United States, support our customers around the world, and contribute to the continued growth of the local economy and innovation community,” said Paul Apen, chief business and operations officer at E Ink Construction is expected to be completed by March 2027 with support from NV5 Planning & Design, Inc., IF Design L.L.C., and SPEC Process Engineering & Construction, Inc.E Ink was spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 1997 and has been headquartered in Billerica since its inception. The post E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: E Ink expanding U.S. HQ in Billerica, MA; 260+ employees, completion March 2027
MIT spinout tech pioneer investing in R&D center strengthens innovation hub footprint
Signals sustained employer confidence in Boston-area life sciences and advanced tech clusters
stories.summary: E Ink, the ePaper technology pioneer spun from MIT, broke ground on an expansion of its Billerica, Massachusetts headquarters and innovation center, which currently houses 260+ employees. The project is slated for completion by March 2027. The expansion underscores E Ink's commitment to U.S. innovation and its role as a key R&D center serving global customers.
stories.impact: Employer expansion in Billerica/Boston signals sustained talent attraction and retention in the Route 128 corridor. This drives housing demand from white-collar tech and life sciences workers seeking to live near advanced-manufacturing and biotech clusters, supporting multifamily rent growth in nearby Boston submarkets (Cambridge, Waltham, Somerville). Window to develop workforce housing before cost competition intensifies.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer announced a joint investment in a $90-million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed, 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego. The borrower, Gemdale USA, will use the proceeds to refinance an existing loan. The four-building lab and office campus in Del Mar Heights is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences, a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. Aperture Del Mar serves as Neurocrine’s mission-critical global headquarters as part of a lease that runs through 2036. The loan is part of Breakthrough’s second life science fund, which held its first close at the end of 2025. Tishman Speyer participated through its recently established debt platform. Breakthrough is a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bello Capital, and has several San Diego-area properties. The post Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer close $90M mezzanine loan for San Diego life science campus
Aperture Del Mar: 538k SF, fully leased to Neurocrine through 2036, mission-critical HQ
Life science debt platform activity confirms capital flowing into biopharm real estate
stories.summary: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer jointly provided a $90 million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego's Del Mar Heights submarket. The property is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences as its mission-critical global headquarters under a lease extending through 2036. The loan is part of Breakthrough's second life science fund and Tishman Speyer's recently launched debt platform.
stories.impact: San Diego life science real estate is attracting institutional capital and long-term anchor tenants with mission-critical leases, signaling stability in the biopharm sector locally. This validates continued demand for worker housing near biotech clusters (Del Mar, UTC, Mission Valley); multifamily developers should prioritize sites near life science employment centers to capture wage-growth-driven rents and lower vacancy risk.

stories.title: MassDOT Seeks Developer for 20-Acre Fall River Site
stories.excerpt: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) on Friday released an Invitation to Bid for the redevelopment of approximately 20 acres of waterfront property along the Taunton River in Fall River. The site represents one of New England’s largest waterfront redevelopment opportunities directly adjacent to commuter rail. Created through the Route 79/Davol Street Corridor Improvements Project and located adjacent to the MBTA’s new Fall River Depot commuter rail station, the site offers a rare opportunity for large-scale, transit-oriented development that can deliver new housing, jobs and long-term economic growth for the South Coast. “We’re turning decades of planning and infrastructure investment into an opportunity to build more housing, create jobs, and reconnect Fall River with its waterfront,” said Gov. Maura Healey. “With South Coast Rail now connecting Fall River to the rest of the region, this site is uniquely positioned for transit-oriented development that will bring new homes, new businesses and new energy to the city.” Interested developers are invited to submit proposals through October 21, 2026. The post MassDOT Seeks Developer for 20-Acre Fall River Site appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MassDOT releases RFB for 20-acre Fall River waterfront site; bids due Oct. 21, 2026
New MBTA Fall River Depot commuter rail station adjacent; Route 79 corridor improvements completed
Transit-oriented development opportunity; Gov. Healey emphasizes housing and job creation on South Coast
stories.summary: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation released a Request for Proposals for redevelopment of approximately 20 acres of waterfront property in Fall River along the Taunton River, directly adjacent to the newly opened MBTA Fall River Depot commuter rail station. The site is one of New England's largest waterfront redevelopment parcels created through the Route 79/Davol Street Corridor Improvements Project. Proposals are due October 21, 2026.
stories.impact: Fall River's new commuter rail connection to the broader MBTA network creates a rare, large-scale transit-oriented development opportunity that will drive population in-migration and job growth on the South Coast. This signals an inflection point for housing demand in a historically distressed market; multifamily developers should prepare for site acquisition and entitlements now, as the South Coast corridor is poised for 5–10-year housing expansion driven by improved regional connectivity and state backing.

stories.title: West Palm Beach Multifamily Property Converted From Condos Sells for $91M
stories.excerpt: The seesaw history of a West Palm Beach residential complex has a new chapter. A joint venture between the Kamson Corporation and Joel Gluck’s Scopus Property Management has closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, Commercial Observer has learned. The 400-unit property was built in 1990 for multifamily usage and later converted to condominiums before it was restored back to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl supplied an $81 million acquisition loan for the property, which encompasses 28 acres on 1401 Village Boulevard. Previous ownership consisted of individual owners of the 400 condo units who decided to terminate the communities’ condominium association last year. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt with a team led by David Bollag and James Darling. “Ponte Verde is a well-located community with strong bones and a clear path forward,” Bollag said in a statement. “Rather than underwriting to where the property had been, [Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl’s] teams focused on the strength and experience of the buyer and the credibility of the business plan, which allowed us to deliver a financing solution on the timeline the transaction required.” The Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes multifamily community consists of 23 two- and three-story garden-style residential buildings totaling roughly 360,488 net rentable square feet, featuring one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Community amenities include a resident clubhouse, two swimming pools, a fitness center, tennis courts, racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, a barbecue area and spa. Prospect Ridge, Blue Owl, the Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kamson/Scopus acquire Ponte Verde (400 units) West Palm Beach for $90M; condo-to-rental conversion
Prospect Ridge, Blue Owl provided $81M loan; property restored to rental in Aug. 2025
Demonstrates institutional appetite for bulk condo-to-rental conversions in South Florida supply crunch
stories.summary: A joint venture of Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, a 400-unit multifamily community in West Palm Beach built in 1990 and previously converted to condominiums. The property was restored to rental housing in August 2025 after individual condo owners voted to terminate the condominium association. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl provided an $81 million acquisition loan.
stories.impact: West Palm Beach's tight rental supply and condo-to-rental conversions signal strong rental demand and pricing power, attracting institutional capital to bulk stabilization deals. However, the conversion path highlights supply fragmentation; multifamily developers should scout pre-conversion condo portfolios and acquire ground-up development sites in West Palm Beach submarkets (Boca Raton, Deerfield Beach) where new construction can outpace conversions and capture rent growth from in-migration and job expansion.

stories.title: Logos Faith Development Sets 15 Groundbreakings Over the Next Three Years
stories.excerpt: Logos Faith Development, a Los Angeles-based affordable housing developer partnering with faith communities across Southern California, announced 15 groundbreakings planned across 2026, 2027 and 2028. In support of that growth, Logos has signed a long-term lease for new headquarters in Downtown Los Angeles. The large-scale development schedule includes five groundbreakings in 2026, five more slated for 2027 and an additional five planned for 2028. The company’s total development pipeline is now valued at roughly $750 million, encompassing more than 2,000 affordable housing units in partnership with over 15 faith-based organizations. Pastor Martin Porter, founder and CEO, Logos Faith Development, said, “Logos Faith Development is moving our headquarters to Downtown Los Angeles from the Culver City area with a long-term lease at 515 South Figueroa. This is a sign that we are confident about the future of DTLA and a central location that will allow our team to support the affordable housing projects underway and planned across SoCal.” The post Logos Faith Development Sets 15 Groundbreakings Over the Next Three Years appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Logos Faith Development plans 15 groundbreakings (2026–2028); $750M pipeline, 2,000+ affordable units
Relocation of HQ to Downtown LA (515 S. Figueroa); partnering with 15+ faith-based organizations
Signals developer confidence in DTLA and affordable-housing funding environment
stories.summary: Logos Faith Development, a Los Angeles-based affordable housing developer, announced 15 planned groundbreakings across 2026–2028 (five per year) with a total pipeline valued at approximately $750 million encompassing 2,000+ affordable units in partnership with 15+ faith-based organizations. The company also signed a long-term lease for new headquarters in Downtown Los Angeles, relocating from Culver City.
stories.impact: Large affordable-housing operator committing to Downtown LA expansion and regional acceleration signals strong public funding (likely Prop HHH, LA's bond measures) and sustained demand for workforce housing across Southern California. Multifamily developers should monitor faith-based and mixed-income project zoning shifts, as Logos' scale and speed may accelerate infill site availability and lower-income renter demand; be prepared to acquire or partner on mixed-income deals in DTLA and LA County infill markets.

stories.title: Housing Development in North Lawndale Breaks Ground
stories.excerpt: Crews recently broke ground on a North Lawndale community, the Trumbull Collection, a group of nine market-rate three-flat apartment buildings. The $6.5 million project will replace eight vacant lots on the 1600 and 1800 blocks of S. Drake Ave. and S. Trumbull Ave. with 27 mid-density homes. The city-backed project is being led by Westside Community Group, a North Lawndale-based real estate development firm. Following completion of the Trumball Collection, the firm intends to lead development of a subsequent 33-unit Missing Middle project in East Garfield Park. “By advancing our local developers’ plans and supporting construction costs, we’re contributing to neighborhood stability, wealth-building opportunities, and ultimately, the development of safer, more affordable communities,” said Mayor Brandon Johnson. The Johnson administration provided approximately $4 million in developmental assistance made available through Mayor Johnson’s $1.25B Housing and Economic Development Bond. The project is one of five Missing Middle projects in North Lawndale. The five minority-led development teams are approved to construct 40 multi-unit buildings valued at $37.7 million. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post Housing Development in North Lawndale Breaks Ground appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: North Lawndale: Trumbull Collection breaks ground; 27 units, 9 three-flats, $6.5M; city backing
Westside Community Group (local developer) leading; $4M city assistance via $1.25B Housing Bond
Five minority-led Missing Middle projects approved for 40 buildings, $37.7M; infill model replicating
stories.summary: Westside Community Group broke ground on the Trumbull Collection in Chicago's North Lawndale neighborhood, a $6.5 million project replacing eight vacant lots with nine market-rate three-flat buildings totaling 27 units. The City of Chicago provided approximately $4 million in development assistance through Mayor Johnson's $1.25 billion Housing and Economic Development Bond. The project is one of five approved Missing Middle developments in North Lawndale, involving five minority-led teams approved to construct 40 multi-unit buildings valued at $37.7 million.
stories.impact: North Lawndale's Missing Middle infill acceleration (27–40 units per project, local developer-led) signals Chicago's sustained commitment to mid-density housing in historically underserved neighborhoods. This creates supply pressure on older, lower-amenity Class B/C assets in adjacent submarkets while opening zoning and financing pathways for developers; multifamily investors should monitor North Lawndale and similar South/West Side corridors for acquisition opportunities and repositioning upside as neighborhood stability and rent growth follow public capital infusion.

stories.title: Waste Management Buys 146-Acre Miami-Dade Development Site for $380M
stories.excerpt: Waste Management has paid nearly $380 million for about 146 acres in Medley, Fla., where the Houston-based company will likely build another landfill, property records show. The land sits parallel to Route 27 at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades national park. About half the site remains vacant while the rest serves as a surface truck parking lot. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management’s 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. An entity tied to Hialeah Gardens-based Lowell Dunn Company sold the land. The same entity provided $366.8 million in seller financing, which is scheduled to mature in 2046. In a recorded easement, Lowell Dunn Company also agreed to allow Waste Management to install underground stormwater pipes across its neighboring property, enabling runoff from Waste Management’s site to discharge into a canal north of the property. Representatives for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deal marks the second acquisition made by a waste management company in Miami-Dade County just this month. Woodlands, Texas-based Waste Connections paid $51 million for a 12-acre surface trucking parking lot in Miami Gardens. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Waste Management acquires 146 acres in Medley, FL for $380M; adjacent to existing 170-acre landfill
Land use: landfill expansion near Everglades, Route 27; seller financing ($366.8M) until 2046
Non-housing industrial/infrastructure investment; limits nearby residential development and property values
stories.summary: Waste Management purchased approximately 146 acres in Medley, Florida for nearly $380 million, where the Houston-based company plans to build another landfill. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management's existing 170-acre Medley Landfill complex near Route 27 and the Everglades. An entity tied to Lowell Dunn Company sold the land and provided $366.8 million in seller financing maturing in 2046.
stories.impact: MINIMAL MULTIFAMILY RELEVANCE. Industrial waste infrastructure investment in exurban Miami-Dade does not create housing demand; landfill expansion typically constrains residential development nearby due to odor, noise, and environmental externalities. Multifamily developers should avoid acquisitions in Medley corridor and focus on other Miami-Dade submarkets (Doral, Wynwood, Allapattah) where amenities and demographics support rent growth.

stories.title: Carlyle Group, Haussmann Submit Plans for 99 Units at Brooklyn’s 566 Grand Avenue
stories.excerpt: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development have plans to partner on a 99-unit apartment complex in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood. The two developers filed plans Thursday with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to bring a new 12-story mixed-use building to 566 Grand Avenue, near the corner of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. Spokespeople for Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building will feature 99 Class A apartments, according to the filing, as well as ground-floor retail space. There will be 10 apartments on the second floor, 11 units each on the third through ninth floors, and four apartments each on floors 10, 11 and 12. The developers also plan to include several in-demand amenities at the property, such as a pet spa, a tenant theater, a game room, a children’s playroom, coworking space, a gym and an outdoor lounge. It is unclear if Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program, which offers developers significant and lengthy tax breaks if their buildings feature a certain percentage of affordable housing. However, the 99-unit plan does provide a clue that this might be the case. A widely unpopular component of the 485-x program is higher construction wage requirements for buildings with 100 or more units. However, buildings with 99 or fewer units that utilize this program are not bound by those wage requirements. Crown Heights has been awash with residential building plans as of late. Avery Hall is planning an 18-story, 250-unit development at 1550 Bedford Avenue, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is looking to build a 300-unit housing development in the neighborhood at 1119 Pacific Street. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Carlyle Group, Haussmann file plans for 99-unit apartment at 566 Grand Ave, Crown Heights, Brooklyn
12-story mixed-use; Class A units, ground-floor retail, premium amenities; zoning compliance unclear
Institutional capital active in Brooklyn infill; 485-x tax abatement eligibility unknown
stories.summary: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed plans with NYC Department of Buildings for a 99-unit Class A apartment complex at 566 Grand Avenue in Brooklyn's Crown Heights neighborhood, near the intersection of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. The planned 12-story mixed-use building will include ground-floor retail and premium amenities (pet spa, theater, game room, gym, coworking). It is unclear whether the developers plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program.
stories.impact: Crown Heights continued institutional development signals sustained Brooklyn demand despite high land costs and entitlement complexity. Tax abatement eligibility and final zoning approval will determine project feasibility and economics; if approved with 485-x, this validates the submarket's supply premium and may accelerate competing ground-up development nearby. Developers should monitor Crown Heights/Prospect Heights infill pipeline for land assembly and conversion opportunities ahead of potential rent growth.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Refis San Diego Apartments With $34M Loan
stories.excerpt: Developer Jeff Svitak has landed $34.25 million of bridge debt for a newly completed San Diego multifamily project, Commercial Observer has learned. Lightstone Capital originated the senior loan for Svitak’s Kaya Apartments development in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood. John Zubak, managing director and head of origination, western region at Lightstone Capital, originated the deal. “From the outset, Kaya has been about creating housing that is deeply connected to the character of Bankers Hill while fostering a true sense of community,” Svitak said in a statement. Located at 2700 Third Avenue, Kaya Apartments debuted last year with 78 units ranging from studios to two bedrooms. Community amenities at the fully-leased complex include coworking space, community lounge, a shared kitchen and on-site café. Lightstone Capital also closed a $23.4 million senior bridge loan in July for Alliance Development Services‘ The Flats at TerraMar multifamily project in Carlsbad, Calif. Located at 5010 Avenida Encinas 32 miles north of San Diego, the 98-unit apartment community with 15 designated as affordable housing will involve converting a former Studio 6 hotel. Last but not least, Lightstone also recently originated a $11.5 million senior bridge loan for Fuller Realty‘s acquisition of an industrial property at 300 S. Sheldon Road in Channelview, Texas. bullets: Lightstone Capital closes $34.25M bridge loan for Kaya Apartments (78 units, San Diego Bankers Hill)
Newly completed, fully leased; studios to 2BR; community-focused design, strong absorption
Smaller-balance acquisition debt available; San Diego market health evident in bridge deployment
stories.summary: Developer Jeff Svitak obtained a $34.25 million senior bridge loan from Lightstone Capital for Kaya Apartments, a newly completed 78-unit multifamily development in San Diego's Bankers Hill neighborhood. The fully leased property features studios to two-bedroom units and community-focused amenities including coworking space, shared kitchen, and on-site café. Lightstone Capital also closed a $23.4 million loan for another San Diego-area multifamily project (The Flats at TerraMar in Carlsbad, 98 units).
stories.impact: Lightstone Capital's consistent deployment of bridge debt to small and mid-size San Diego operators signals lender confidence in the market's fundamentals (strong absorption, pricing power) and lower refinance risk. This validates continued development feasibility in San Diego infill submarkets (Bankers Hill, Carlsbad) even with moderating transaction volume; multifamily developers should refinance or dispose of bridge positions before rate repricing and prioritize lease-up velocity to demonstrate exit optionality.

stories.title: Rexford Plans Up to $2B in Sales After Posting $507M Loss in Q2
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is dramatically accelerating its shift from being the most aggressive industrial buyer in Southern California into perhaps the region’s biggest seller. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has identified about $2 billion of “noncore assets” for disposition as it continues to prioritize keeping tenants in Rexford buildings. That property sales forecast is sharply up from the previous range of $400 million to $500 million. During the REIT’s earnings call Friday, CEO Laura Clark said the disposition pool encompasses about 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market — generally by more than 20 percent. Chief Financial Officer Michael Fitzmaurice said about $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, rather than refinance into a higher rate environment. The remaining proceeds will be guided by market conditions. “We’re not de-levering to sit idle; we’re de-levering to redeploy,” Fitzmaurice said. The vast majority of Rexford’s property sales are expected to close before the end of the year. “We expect that pricing will be achieved at levels that allow us to redeploy proceeds on a neutral to accretive basis through our 2027 FFO per share, and this is not a dilutive exercise,” Clark said. Rexford said it sold seven properties totaling approximately 572,000 square feet for $137.9 million during the second quarter, after disposing of five properties for $127.4 million in the first quarter. The company previously known for 10-figure buying sprees has completed no acquisitions this year. Rexford plans to use property sales proceeds to repay debt, repurchase shares and pursue higher-yielding investments. It bought back $100 million of stock during the quarter, bringing its 2026 repurchases to $300 million, and its board subsequently authorized a new $1 billion repurchase program. The ramped-up disposition strategy also came with a $506.9 million
bullets: Rexford Industrial increases noncore asset sales target to ~$2B (from $400–500M); 8M SF identified
Properties: limited value creation, rents 20%+ above market, shorter lease terms; ~$1B to repay 2027 debt
Industrial REIT portfolio de-leveraging and redeployment; soft signal on Southern California market saturation
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty sharply increased its noncore asset disposition forecast to approximately $2 billion, up from the prior $400–500 million guidance, comprising about 8 million square feet. CEO Laura Clark characterized the portfolio as having limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market (generally >20%). CFO Michael Fitzmaurice noted that roughly $1 billion of sale proceeds will repay debt maturing in 2027, while the remainder will be redeployed based on market conditions.
stories.impact: Rexford's dramatic portfolio shift from acquisition-mode to disposition—targeting overvalued, above-market industrial assets—signals market saturation in Southern California industrial real estate and higher debt service costs. While this is an industrial-focused play, it reflects broader Southern California capital constraints and higher discount rates; multifamily developers should monitor refinancing windows (2027 debt maturity, rising cost of capital) and prepare for potential distressed asset availability in mixed-use or opportunity-zone parcels as industrial players de-lever.
